rule_en: Year-count ('transmission'): divide the current year of life by 12 and count the remainder from a starting point, counting the starting sign as 1. Worked example: 35th year, remainder 11, counted from Virgo (Ascendant and Mars), reaches Cancer (Saturn). This equals one sign per year: sign = start + (completed years mod 12).
locator: Valens IV.11 'The Operative Year and the Method of Fractions'; Riley tr. printed p.78 (PDF p.80); nearest preceding markers Kroll p.174, Pingree p.164
notes: Inclusive counting is confirmed by the example (Virgo=1 … Cancer=11). Valens frames it as one star 'transmitting' the year to another, not as a single 'lord of the year'.

rule_en: Count the years from the Sun, the Moon and the Ascendant. If the count ends in an empty sign, the year is handed to that sign's ruler. Also count from Fortune, Daimon, Love and Necessity. Counting from the angles is 'more scientific'.

rule_en: 'Under the rays of the sun' weakens a significator (e.g. ruler of the Lot or Ascendant in VIII under the rays = poverty). Riley's Valens gives NO numerical threshold (no 15° rule).
locator: Valens II.8K;9P 'The VIII Place of Death'; Riley tr. printed p.28 (PDF p.30); nearest preceding markers Kroll p.64, Pingree p.62
notes: Searched the whole text for 15°, 'beams', 'rays', 'degrees from the sun'. No orb for being under the beams was found. Any 15° rule must come from another source and be labelled as such.

rule_en: A new Moon under the Sun's rays cannot be the apheta (releaser) unless exactly on the Ascendant degree.
locator: Valens III.1 'The Control'; Riley tr. printed p.58 (PDF p.60); nearest preceding markers Kroll p.133, Pingree p.126
quote_withheld: Riley translation in copyright: see the locator

rule_en: Moon's invisibility before conjunction: it becomes invisible at a distance before the Sun equal to half the rising time of the Sun's sign (e.g. Sun in Aries, klima 2: rising time 20, so invisible from 10° before the Sun).
locator: Valens I.14K;13P 'The Invisibility Period of the Moon'; Riley tr. printed p.13 (PDF p.15); nearest preceding markers Kroll p.28, Pingree p.27
notes: This is a visibility rule for the Moon only, not a general under-the-beams orb.
quote_withheld: Riley translation in copyright: see the locator

rule_en: Eleven lunar phases by elongation from the Sun: new; first visibility; crescent 45°; quarter 90°; gibbous 135°; full 180°; second gibbous 225°; second quarter 270°; second crescent 315°; final visibility 360°; plus a phase 'when it first begins to wane'.
locator: Valens II.35K;36P 'The Eleven Phases of the Moon and The Influence of Their Effects'; Riley tr. printed p.46 (PDF p.48); nearest preceding markers Kroll p.106, Pingree p.101
notes: Significations follow, e.g. new moon = rank and power; first visibility = life, occupation, wealth; quarter = injuries, diseases; full = fame and infamy.

rule_en: Only the waxing Moon rejoices in the VIII place.
locator: Valens II.8K;9P; Riley tr. printed p.28 (PDF p.30); nearest preceding markers Kroll p.64, Pingree p.63

rule_en: In the year's distribution, stars past the first station (retrograde) delay matters; opposite the Sun they are weak; at the second station they cancel delay; at last visibility they bring obstacles and illness.
locator: Valens IV.14 'The Phases and Transits of the Stars'; Riley tr. printed p.82 (PDF p.84); nearest preceding markers Kroll p.182, Pingree p.173
